name: Amazon Redshift
model: Tables of typed columns, PostgreSQL-flavoured SQL (forked from Postgres 8.0.2); AWS data warehouse, provisioned or serverless
engine_note: Massively parallel columnar store; RA3 nodes and Serverless keep data in managed storage on S3 with local SSD caching
consistency: Multi-statement transactions. Two levels: SNAPSHOT isolation (default for new clusters and serverless) or SERIALIZABLE (option; rejects write skew by cancelling a concurrent transaction). System catalog tables run read committed.
scaling: Provisioned: add or resize nodes (MPP, data distributed by key); RA3 separates compute from managed storage; Serverless scales compute automatically; concurrency scaling adds clusters.
version_note: Patch 205 on the CURRENT track: Iceberg materialized views, zero-ETL improvements, post-quantum hybrid TLS key exchange.
reach: Reach for it when your data and pipelines are in AWS and you want a SQL warehouse that loads from S3 and zero-ETL from Aurora or DynamoDB.
avoid: Avoid for per-request app queries or many tiny writes; and note Python UDFs reach end of support after June 30, 2026.
escape: warehouse-scale SQL on AWS with zero-ETL feeds from the app database, without overloading it
chat: Warehouse copy of chats and usage events, fed by zero-ETL from Aurora Postgres, for analytics.
notes: Correction to common lore: SERIALIZABLE is no longer the default; the isolation page (fetched 2026-10-04) says SNAPSHOT is the default for new provisioned clusters and serverless workgroups. Python UDF end of support after 2026-06-30 is from the banner on the same page (AWS blog 2025-06-30). 'Forked from Postgres 8.0.2' is from the Redshift-and-PostgreSQL docs page, not re-fetched today.
